concept_html:
The model registry turns logged models into named, numbered versions. Each log_model(..., registered_model_name="churn_model") or mlflow.register_model(...) call creates a new version: 1, 2, 3. A version never changes. It points at one run, one set of parameters and one model file.

Aliases are movable labels on versions. MLflow 3.16:

from mlflow import MlflowClient

client = MlflowClient()
client.set_registered_model_alias("churn_model", "champion", "3")
model = mlflow.pyfunc.load_model("models:/churn_model@champion")

The scoring job always loads @champion. Promotion moves the alias to a new version. Rollback moves it back. The job's code never changes, and every prediction can be traced to a version and its run.

Stages (Staging, Production, Archived) are the older mechanism. transition_model_version_stage has been deprecated since MLflow 2.9, and MLflow 3.16 warns that stages will be removed. Models in Unity Catalog on Databricks use aliases only, with three-level names such as ml.churn.churn_model after mlflow.set_registry_uri("databricks-uc").

Promote on evidence, not by hand:

  1. Train and register a candidate version.
  2. Evaluate it on the same held-out data and metric as the current champion.
  3. Move champion only if the candidate beats it by a margin agreed in advance.
  4. Keep the old version reachable, for example with a previous_champion alias, so rollback is one call.

Record the decision: which versions were compared, the scores and who approved. On Databricks, Unity Catalog grants (lesson A4-L2) control who can move an alias.

lines: from __future__ import annotations
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
from mlflow import MlflowClient
def promote_if_better(client: MlflowClient, name: str, candidate: str, metric: str, min_gain: float) -> bool:
"""Move the champion alias to candidate if it beats the champion by min_gain."""
champ = client.get_model_version_by_alias(name, "champion")
champ_score = client.get_run(champ.run_id).data.metrics[metric]
cand_score = client.get_run(client.get_model_version(name, candidate).run_id).data.metrics[metric]
if cand_score < champ_score + min_gain:
client.set_registered_model_alias(name, "previous_champion", champ.version)
client.set_registered_model_alias(name, "champion", candidate)

exercises.prompt:
Write `promote_if_better(client, name, candidate, metric, min_gain) -> bool`. The model already has a `champion` alias.

- Read the champion with `client.get_model_version_by_alias(name, "champion")`, and its score from `client.get_run(champ.run_id).data.metrics[metric]`.
- Read the candidate's score through `client.get_model_version(name, candidate)`.
- If the candidate's score is at least the champion's plus `min_gain`, set `previous_champion` to the champion's version, then `champion` to `candidate`, and return `True`. Otherwise change nothing and return `False`.

The checker passes a stub client with the same methods as `MlflowClient`.
exercises.prompt_html:
Write promote_if_better(client, name, candidate, metric, min_gain) -> bool. The model already has a champion alias.

  • Read the champion with client.get_model_version_by_alias(name, "champion"), and its score from client.get_run(champ.run_id).data.metrics[metric].
  • Read the candidate's score through client.get_model_version(name, candidate).
  • If the candidate's score is at least the champion's plus min_gain, set previous_champion to the champion's version, then champion to candidate, and return True. Otherwise change nothing and return False.

The checker passes a stub client with the same methods as MlflowClient.
exercises.solution:
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from mlflow import MlflowClient


def promote_if_better(client: MlflowClient, name: str, candidate: str, metric: str, min_gain: float) -> bool:
    """Move the champion alias to candidate if it beats the champion by min_gain.

    Args:
        client: MLflow client, or any object with the same methods.
        name: Registered model name.
        candidate: Candidate version number, as a string.
        metric: Run metric to compare, higher is better.
        min_gain: Smallest improvement that justifies promotion.

    Returns:
        True if the alias moved.
    """
    champ = client.get_model_version_by_alias(name, "champion")
    champ_score = client.get_run(champ.run_id).data.metrics[metric]
    cand_score = client.get_run(client.get_model_version(name, candidate).run_id).data.metrics[metric]
    if cand_score < champ_score + min_gain:
        return False
    client.set_registered_model_alias(name, "previous_champion", champ.version)
    client.set_registered_model_alias(name, "champion", candidate)
    return True

title: Registry versions and aliases, not stages
why_html: A team kept production models as files named model_prod.pkl, overwritten on each release. A new version cut conversion forecasts by 12% overnight. Rolling back meant finding last month's file on someone's laptop. It took a day. With versions and an alias, rollback is set_registered_model_alias("churn_model", "champion", "4"), and the scoring job picks it up on its next run.
